text: Be yourself; everyone else is already taken.
author: Oscar Wilde
note: ATTRIBUTION DISPUTED. Universally credited to Wilde; not found in any of his published works, letters or recorded conversation. First traced to the late 20th century. This is the site's motto — decide whether to keep it attributed, run it unattributed as a phrase, or retire it.

text: We are all in the gutter, but some of us are looking at the stars.
author: Oscar Wilde

text: A cynic is a man who knows the price of everything and the value of nothing.
author: Oscar Wilde

text: The truth is rarely pure and never simple.
author: Oscar Wilde
source: The Importance of Being Earnest, Act I

text: Price is nothing. Value is everything.
Well done is better than well said.
author: Benjamin Franklin

text: To be yourself in a world that is constantly trying to make you something else is the greatest accomplishment.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
note: ATTRIBUTION DISPUTED. Universally credited to Emerson; not found in his published works. Also circulates as e.e. cummings. No primary source.

text: Live in the sunshine, swim the sea, drink the wild air.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

text: What you do speaks so loudly that I cannot hear what you say.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

text: Nothing great was ever achieved without enthusiasm.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

text: The greater danger for most of us lies not in setting our aim too high and falling short, but in setting our aim too low, and achieving our mark.
author: Michelangelo
note: ATTRIBUTION DISPUTED. No primary source in Michelangelo's letters or poems; appears to be 20th-century. Also the longest line here at 29 words.

text: In theory, there is no difference between theory and practice. But in practice, there is.
author: Yogi Berra
note: Attributed to Berra, but also to Van de Snepscheut and others. No primary source.

text: I find that the harder I work, the more luck I seem to have.
author: Thomas Jefferson
note: ATTRIBUTION DISPUTED. The Jefferson Foundation lists this as spurious — not found in his papers. Older versions run to Coleman Cox (1922).

text: Never interrupt your enemy when he is making a mistake.
author: Napoleon Bonaparte
note: ATTRIBUTION DISPUTED. Universally credited to Napoleon; no primary source in his correspondence.

text: Let us never negotiate out of fear. But let us never fear to negotiate.
author: John F. Kennedy

text: History doesn't repeat itself, but it does rhyme.
author: Mark Twain
note: ATTRIBUTION DISPUTED. Not found in Twain. The Mark Twain Project lists it as unverified.

text: And, when you want something, all the universe conspires in helping you to achieve it.
author: Paulo Coelho
